fields.description: MASSPIRG is the Massachusetts arm of the Public Interest Research Group network; its researchers, advocates and organizers work on consumer and public-health issues, including zero-waste, plastics, PFAS and safe drinking water bills at the State House.

projects.name: Getting to Zero Waste bills
projects.description: Pushes 2025-2026 bills to expand the Bottle Bill to water bottles and nips, restrict single-use plastic bags and ban most polystyrene foam containers.

projects.name: Clean water and toxic chemicals bills
projects.description: Backs bills to phase out PFAS in consumer products, require lead filters for school drinking water and disclose toxic chemicals in children's products.

actions.name: Take action with MASSPIRG
actions.description: Sign MASSPIRG's current petitions, including ones on plastic packaging, PFAS and microplastics.

fields.description: Western Massachusetts local group of Extinction Rebellion, the climate movement that uses nonviolent direct action; it organizes through an email list and social media.

actions.name: Join the XR Western Mass email list
actions.description: Sign up to get updates and get involved with Extinction Rebellion in Western Massachusetts.

fields.description: Boston hub of the Sunrise Movement, the national youth movement working to stop climate change, get fossil fuel money out of politics and elect climate leaders.

Grassroots statewide climate network, part of Better Future Project, that works to end fossil fuel dependence and win a just transition through statewide working groups and local member-led chapters called nodes.

events.name: Save Money with Clean Heat 2.0 Brainstorm
events.description: Brainstorm on what a second Save Money with Clean Heat campaign could look like.

events.name: March in the HONK! Parade
events.location: Day St and Herbert St parking lots, Davis Square, Somerville
events.description: 350 Mass marches in the HONK! activist street-band parade from Davis Square to Harvard Square; arrive by 11 AM.

events.name: Climate Justice: A Primer
events.description: Online workshop on how climate change hits communities unequally and how to organize with frontline communities.

actions.name: Join a 350 Mass working group
actions.description: Volunteer with a statewide working group such as Clean the Grid, Transportation, Science, Media Engagement, Stop and Steer the Money, Climate & Democracy or the Statewide Legislative Team.

actions.name: Join your local 350 Mass node
actions.description: Get involved with a member-led local chapter of 350 Mass near you.

events.name: Decarbonizing: the Data with Professor Zana Cranmer
events.description: Online talk on what municipal adoption data for solar, heat pumps and electric vehicles can teach local climate groups.

fields.description: Berkshire-based creative studio started in 1989 that makes films, animation, design and books, including videos for nonprofits and an environmental film festival.

actions.name: Request a free climate speaker
actions.description: Schools, groups and businesses can ask the chapter for a free speaker presentation on the climate crisis.

events.name: Stop the Madness in Washington
events.description: Protest against war spending and for human needs, peace, justice, democracy and a livable planet; rescheduled from September 26.

events.name: Watertown Faces Climate Change meeting
events.location: Watertown (in person with a hybrid option; details emailed before each meeting)
events.description: Regular meeting of the group's climate working group, which works on cutting emissions from buildings and vehicles in Watertown.

projects.name: Watertown Faces Climate Change
projects.description: Working group (and 350 Mass node) that helps the city carry out its 2022 Climate and Energy Plan and looks for ways to cut emissions from buildings and vehicles.

projects.name: Life-Friendly Garden Tour
projects.description: Annual tour of Watertown gardens that are cared for without chemicals; the fall 2025 tour focused on dealing with rabbits and rodents without poisons.

events.name: Shut Down ICE Week of Action: environmental and immigration justice day
events.description: 350Vermont joins the Shut Down ICE week of action in Williston for a day on the links between environmental justice and immigration justice (10 AM-12 PM and 2-4 PM).

events.name: Campaign Planning & Strategy Training
events.description: Online training on how organizing campaigns work and how to set campaign goals, for people who want to propose a 350Vermont campaign for 2027.

events.name: Families Rise Up monthly meeting
events.location: Unitarian Church of Montpelier, 130 Main St, Montpelier, VT
events.recurrence: Third Saturday of the month, 10 AM-12 PM
events.description: Monthly gathering of families working on climate action, with snacks and childcare support.

events.name: Chittenden Node Meeting
events.location: 239 S Union St, Burlington, VT (or Zoom)
events.recurrence: Fourth Monday of the month, 7 PM
events.description: Monthly meeting of 350Vermont's Chittenden County local group.

projects.name: Peakbusting
projects.description: Volunteers gather with neighbors to cut electricity use during grid demand peaks, to help retire polluting peaker plants, working with No Coal No Gas.

projects.name: Electric Ratepayer Protection (H.753)
projects.description: Campaign for a ratepayer protection program to lower electric bills for low-income households so they can switch heating and transportation to electricity.

projects.name: Don't Burn Our Future
projects.description: Local groups and allies oppose expanding the McNeil biomass plant in Burlington and a proposed new biomass plant in Lyndonville.

projects.name: Community Weatherization
projects.description: Local groups support weatherization programs and organize hands-on work parties to insulate and air-seal Vermont homes.

actions.name: Join the Transportation Working Group
actions.description: Volunteer group supporting Green Mountain Transit; meets most Wednesdays 7-8 PM, hybrid, at the 350VT office in Burlington.
